title: FDA De Novo review of IDx-DR: autonomous AI detects diabetic retinopathy in a 900-person primary care trial
summary: In the trial that FDA reviewed for the IDx-DR De Novo grant, the AI found more than mild diabetic retinopathy with 87.4% sensitivity and 89.5% specificity in primary care.
account: IDx, LLC of Coralville, Iowa, tested its IDx-DR software in a pivotal trial that enrolled 900 adults with diabetes at 10 primary care sites in the United States between January and July 2017. Camera operators with no earlier imaging experience, trained to a standard protocol, took four retinal photographs with a Topcon NW400 camera, and the software decided on its own whether more than mild diabetic retinopathy was present. A reading center graded separate images of the same eyes, taken by a professional photographer, as the reference standard. FDA reviewers report that the software found 173 of 198 people with the disease, an observed sensitivity of 87.4%, and that its observed specificity was 89.5%. It gave a usable result for 96.1% of participants with a reading center grade. FDA granted the De Novo request on 11 April 2018 and found that the probable benefits outweigh the probable risks. The trial measured accuracy against a reference standard. It did not measure vision outcomes, and 73 of the 892 participants who completed the procedures could not be fully analyzed.
purpose: IDx-DR was built to detect more than mild diabetic retinopathy in primary care without a physician reading the images. The measured benefit is that purpose.
deployer: Ten primary care sites in the IDx-DR pivotal trial
location: Ten primary care sites, United States

ratings.reason: Camera operators with no earlier imaging experience obtained a screening result for 96.1% of graded participants, and the software found 87.4% of people with more than mild retinopathy.
FDA reviewers describe wider access to retinopathy screening in primary care as a potential benefit, and no realized effect on access or vision across the population is reported.
